name: Diagnose the incomplete eval plan
note: Each plan sounds reasonable but has one critical gap that the guide already taught you to catch. Find it.

items.prompt: Model B scores one point higher than model A on our benchmark, so we'll ship B.
candidates: No confidence interval — a one-point lead on one run may be noise
We didn't try a model C
items.correct: No confidence interval — a one-point lead on one run may be noise
items.explanation: A one-point difference with no sense of variance is a coin-flip. Pair the comparison and bootstrap the difference (Chapter 3): if the 95% CI on B−A straddles zero, you'd be shipping noise.
items.principle: Never act on a model comparison without an interval on the difference.

items.prompt: We passed offline evaluation at 0.88, so the feature is done — ship it and move on.
candidates: Offline is a launch gate, not a guarantee — add live guardrails and drift monitoring
We should have used a different metric
items.correct: Offline is a launch gate, not a guarantee — add live guardrails and drift monitoring
items.explanation: A frozen offline metric can't move when production drifts (Chapter 11). Without live guardrails (override rate, latency, cost) and drift detection, a regression on real traffic is invisible until users complain.
items.principle: Evaluation is continuous: offline gates launch, monitoring keeps it honest.

items.prompt: Our customer-support RAG bot tops the MMLU leaderboard, so it's ready for customers.
candidates: MMLU doesn't measure RAG faithfulness on your docs — build a domain eval
The bot needs a bigger context window
items.correct: MMLU doesn't measure RAG faithfulness on your docs — build a domain eval
items.explanation: MMLU is exam trivia; a support bot's job is grounded answers from your documents. That's a construct-validity miss (Chapter 8): you need a domain eval set measuring retrieval (precision/recall@k) and faithfulness (Chapter 9), not a generic leaderboard.
items.principle: Evaluate the construct your system actually performs, on data that looks like its job.
